items.title: The Small Bottleneck with a Big Impact: Why Automating Box Opening Could Be the Next Frontier in Warehouse Productivity
items.description: When supply chain leaders discuss warehouse automation, the conversation typically centers on high-profile technologies. Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS), robotic picking, sortation systems, artificial intelligence, and digital twins tend to dominate both investment discussions and industry headlines. Yet some of the most significant productivity opportunities are not found in billion-dollar […] The post The Small Bottleneck with a Big Impact: Why Automating Box Opening Could Be the Next Frontier in Warehouse Productivity appeared first on Logisti
items.excerpt:
When supply chain leaders discuss warehouse automation, the conversation typically centers on high-profile technologies. Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS), robotic picking, sortation systems, artificial intelligence, and digital twins tend to dominate both investment discussions and industry headlines. Yet some of the most significant productivity opportunities are not found in billion-dollar distribution center transformations. They are hidden in the seemingly mundane processes that occur thousands of times each day. One such process is carton opening.
At first glance, box cutting appears too simple to warrant strategic attention. Warehouses have been opening cartons manually for decades. Associates use box cutters, inventory moves downstream, and operations continue. But as distribution centers become increasingly automated, manually opening inbound cartons stands out as an area where yesterday’s processes often collide with today’s performance expectations. The question is not whether organizations can automate carton opening. The more interesting question is whether small workflow improvements can generate disproportionate gains in safety, productivity, and return on investment.
Warehouse operators continuously focus on eliminating bottlenecks. Traditionally, attention gravitates toward activities that are highly visible or capital intensive. Storage density, picking productivity, transportation optimization, and labor availability often become top priorities. Yet operational performance is ultimately the sum of thousands of individual activities. A two-second delay repeated 50,000 times per month becomes a significant loss of productive capacity. Similarly, a task that introduces variability, safety risks, or rework can create ripple effects that extend well beyond the activity itself. Manual carton opening falls into this category.
Inbound receiving operations depend on a predictable flow of goods into inspection, decanting, storage, quality control, and fulfillment processes. When carton opening relies entirely on manual labor, performance can vary significantly between operators, shifts, packaging types, and facility conditions. These variations may seem insignificant individually. Collectively, they introduce friction into an environment where efficiency increasingly determines competitive advantage.

items.title: Superhuman Hardware Design Is The Easy Part
items.description: The interface between the digital and physical world is lossy
items.excerpt:
We’re excited to announce that Orchestra Bio has been acquired by OpenAI . To read more about the acquisition, read Jay Rughani and Jorge Conde ’s post about it here . For more general information on what OpenAI is up to in the Health space, check out our podcast with them here .
It took me eight months to build my first FPV drone. I procured the parts in January, received them in February, remembered I bought them in June, assembled and lit the drone on fire in July, re-assembled and crashed it into my neighbor’s roof in August, and then, and only then, at the behest of my wife, downloaded a FPV flight simulator.
A super-intelligent AI surely could have done better.
While far from superhuman today, the frontier models can now generate CAD, design custom PCBs, source COTS parts, and describe how those parts are to be assembled. And they’re only getting better. Hardware design benchmarks like CAD Arena , EE Bench , and my own LuxoBench show steady improvements; and more generally, you’d have to be crazy to bet against the Bitter Lesson and say hardware design will forever stay beyond the frontier.
Superhuman hardware engineers are coming soon , perhaps very soon. But what will they look like? Will superhuman hardware engineers surpass all humans in one fell swoop, or only in specific domains/disciplines? And what will hardware engineering look like before, during, and after the crossover?
My answer to each of these questions starts with one simple observation: that the interface between the digital and physical world is lossy. This makes it hard to “write” changes from the digital world of bits into the physical world of atoms, and hard to “read” measurements of the physical world back into a computer. This lossiness will shape when and how future superhuman hardware engineers will emerge — and means that even once the models can consistently one-shot electromechanical designs , they will still have a lot more work to do .

items.title: The Decision Bottleneck Is Becoming a Logistics Capacity Constraint
items.description: Decision speed matters because logistics capacity can be constrained by queues of unresolved choices just as surely as by a shortage of trucks, doors, labor, or inventory. The important mechanism is the decision bottleneck: work waits while people assemble context, negotiate tradeoffs, secure authority, and… The post The Decision Bottleneck Is Becoming a Logistics Capacity Constraint appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Decision speed matters because logistics capacity can be constrained by queues of unresolved choices just as surely as by a shortage of trucks, doors, labor, or inventory. The important mechanism is the decision bottleneck: work waits while people assemble context, negotiate tradeoffs, secure authority, and translate a choice into action.
A logistics network may have available trucks, open dock doors, sufficient warehouse labor, and inventory on hand and still fail to use that capacity effectively because nobody can make the necessary decision in time. The bottleneck is visible in the earlier decision-to-action chain , where waiting can accumulate across context assembly, analysis, approval, and execution even when the physical assets themselves remain available.
That sounds like a management problem. Increasingly, it is an operating-capacity problem. Logistics capacity is normally expressed in physical terms: trucks, trailers, drivers, dock doors, labor hours, storage positions, conveyor throughput, cubic space, and miles of network infrastructure.
Those measures remain essential. But as logistics becomes more dynamic and more observable, another resource becomes increasingly important: the ability to make and execute decisions at the speed of the operation.
The physical system may have several feasible responses. The warehouse could move the appointment. Labor could be reassigned. Another shipment could be prioritized. A downstream load could be changed. An alternate source of inventory might be available.
But those options have no value if the exception sits in a queue while someone gathers information and seeks approval. During that delay, doors can sit idle, labor can wait, trailers can dwell, and customer commitments can deteriorate. Decision latency converts theoretical physical capacity into unusable capacity.
Many logistics operations have a queue that is not represented on a facility drawing or network model: the queue of unresolved decisions. Planners work through alerts, emails, calls, messages, dashboards, and system worklists. Some issues require seconds. Others require research across multiple systems and coordination with several parties. When exception arrival exceeds decision-processing capacity, the queue grows.
This is operationally similar to any other bottleneck. Work accumulates in front of a constrained resource.
Experienced logistics professionals are high-value resources, yet many organizations use them as integration middleware.

items.title: Latest open artifacts (#25): DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, American-made models, and new regulatory controls in the US & China
items.description: Western open models strike back
items.excerpt:
The geopolitics of open-weight AI are accelerating again this fall, as we would expect with the risks of all AI systems (open and closed) rising rapidly. We’ve seen many news items in the last week showing both the U.S. and Chinese governments positioning themselves for some controls on open models.
MOFCOM, the Ministry of Commerce of the People’s Republic of China, released a policy proposal (it’s not yet a law) that would require frontier AI models and some other technologies to get pre-approval from the government before they can be shared internationally. We found the reaction to this to be overblown – as the document states that open-source technologies will be set up for automatic approvals – but many in geopolitical circles say this is a big deal because it proposes a regulatory framework that could be used in the future to regulate China’s AI industry. Others we trust on this issue say this proposal could be more about preventing issues like the sale of Chinese startup Manus to Western companies, rather than being about frontier AI models. Either way, the wheels of control are moving around AI, and open-weight models are not free from any influence.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released an order on DeepSeek , which restricts DeepSeek itself, as a company, and DeepSeek’s models, as a technology platform, from being a vendor in federal civilian procurement. It is not clear how this will relate to finetuned models or models trained on the outputs of DeepSeek (e.g., Nvidia’s Nemotron models have long relied heavily on DeepSeek models in their training recipes – will they be banned?), but this is an expected action and reinforces the need for a domestic open model ecosystem. Other model makers in China, such as Zhipu AI, makers of GLM, are already on the Entity List under Commerce/BIS, which restricts their access to American technology.
DeepSeek followed the above news up by releasing their internal inference stack publicly, DeepInfer , which is likely far more efficient than existing open-source tools like vLLM/SGLang for their models. Estimates point to DeepSeek making up to 90% gross margin when selling tokens on this inference stack. It is well-known that the top AI labs have much more inference-efficient tools internally, and this is the first time we’ve seen a leading lab share them. items.excerpt:
Warehouse robotics company Exotec has announced the commissioning of two new Skypod systems in Japan with Mitsubishi Shokuhin, a major food distributor, and Trusco Nakayama, one of Japan’s leading industrial distributors.
Deployed in partnership with IHI Logistics Industrial Systems, the new systems further strengthen Exotec’s presence in one of the world’s most advanced markets for logistics automation.
Mitsubishi Shokuhin has commissioned Skypod at its new Food Service Distribution Centre (FSDC) in Soka. The site manages almost 13,000 product references, including food products, alcoholic beverages and professional supplies.
With labour shortages and the need to improve working conditions in its warehouses, Mitsubishi Shokuhin implemented Skypod to reduce operator travel distances, improve picking efficiency, automate ambient temperature operations and maintain a high level of customer service.
The project is part of a broader strategy to build a logistics infrastructure capable of supporting the company’s growth through 2040. The deployment marks an important milestone, as it is the first implementation of Skypod in Japan’s food distribution sector.
Trusco Nakayama also strengthened its industrial logistics capacity with the Exotec Skypod system being fully operational at the group’s new Planet Aichi logistics centre, its largest logistics facility.
Covering approximately 89,000 square meters, the site was designed to support the continued growth of the number of stored product references, which is expected to exceed one million SKUs in the coming years.
Skypod was implemented to automate order fulfilment operations for tools, consumables, safety equipment and industrial supplies. The deployed system includes nearly 32,000 bins, 37 robots and four picking stations to improve productivity, picking accuracy and storage space utilisation.
Both projects highlight the growing adoption of warehouse automation technologies in Japan to address shared challenges, including labour shortages, increasing throughput requirements, improved productivity and better working conditions for warehouse operators.
Romain Moulin, CEO of Exotec, says: “Japan is one of the world’s most demanding and innovative markets when it comes to logistics. The new systems at Mitsubishi Shokuhin and Trusco Nakayama demonstrate Skypod’s ability to meet very different requirements while providing a concrete response to the challenges of productivity, labour availability and service quality.

items.excerpt:
Most organizations don’t have a shortage of dashboards. They have too many. Over the years, reports accumulate – built for a specific meeting, a departed manager, a project that ended, or a question nobody asks anymore. The BI platform fills up with hundreds of assets, and nobody is quite sure which ones matter.
Meanwhile, the people who need data to make decisions still export to spreadsheets, ask analysts for one-off numbers, or rely on intuition.
A dashboard audit is often the first and most useful step in data visualization consulting . It looks at what exists, what’s used, what’s trusted, and what’s missing – and produces a clear plan for fixing it.
Building new dashboards on top of a messy reporting landscape adds to the problem. An audit creates clarity first:
The answers shape everything that follows – what to retire, what to fix, what to consolidate, and what to build.
Most BI platforms record who views what and how often. This data is usually revealing. It’s common to find that a small fraction of dashboards accounts for most of the views, while many others haven’t been opened in months.
Unused dashboards aren’t harmless. They consume refresh capacity, create confusion about which report is authoritative, and make it harder to find what matters.
Every dashboard should support a specific decision or monitoring need. Through interviews, the audit maps dashboards to their intended users and decisions. Assets with no clear purpose or owner are candidates for retirement.
Interviews also reveal gaps: decisions people make regularly without adequate data.
If the same metric shows different values in different reports, users stop trusting all of them. The audit compares key metrics across reports and reviews how they’re calculated. Common culprits include different date logic, different filters, inconsistent handling of returns or cancellations, and different source systems.
Even accurate dashboards fail if users can’t quickly find what they need. Design review looks at layout, chart choice, use of color, information density, labeling, and navigation. Watching real users try to answer a specific question with a dashboard is often more revealing than any checklist.
Common findings include too many charts on one page, unclear titles, missing context such as targets or prior-period comparisons, and decorative visuals that obscure the data.

items.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
items.excerpt:
Today we’re introducing FairStress , a benchmark for measuring demographic fairness in LLMs beyond the choice a model ultimately makes in decisions impacting people. FairStress is available for download, and we’re also building it into Olmo-eval , our open workbench for running and comparing model evaluations.
Models are increasingly being used in high-stakes settings where their outputs can affect people’s opportunities, resources, and care, from screening job applicants and approving loans to prioritizing patients for treatment and evaluating students for admissions. Standard demographic fairness benchmarks often test whether a model selects the same candidate in otherwise identical scenarios after the candidates’ demographic identities are swapped. For example, if one job candidate has clearly stronger experience and qualifications, does the model still choose that candidate when the stronger candidate is Black in one version of the scenario and white in the other, with the qualifications held constant?
Arriving at the same answer in two versions of a scenario can hide meaningful differences in how readily a model changes that decision when challenged, however. Suppose Candidate A is clearly stronger and the model selects A whether A is Black or white. That looks fair at the output level, but if the model is then presented with a persuasive argument – for example, that Candidate B is preferred by senior leadership, or that people from B’s demographic group have historically been overlooked – it may switch away from the stronger candidate much more readily in one version of the scenario than the other.
FairStress is designed to measure these hidden asymmetries.
Across open-weight and frontier models including Olmo, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Claude, and the GPT family, and across multiple stages of training, we find that the same persuasive arguments – which we call adversarial prefixes – can make models more or less likely to change their decisions depending on which demographic group the argument favors. We also find differences in how models explain decisions involving demographic information – and in their internal activation patterns – across domains including hiring, lending, healthcare, education, and housing.

Google TPU 在 Google 内外都已被非常成功地用于大规模训练和部署大型机器学习模型。它们专为机器学习而设计，因此在性能、能耗和成本方面具有显著优势。尽管 TPU 历史上一直与 TensorFlow 和 JAX 生态系统相关联，我们很高兴推出 TorchTPU ——这是 Google 于 2025 年中启动、与 Meta 的 PyTorch 团队合作开展的新项目，旨在让 PyTorch 原生运行在 TPU 上。
为了在 Python 框架之下对 Google TPU 进行编程，开发者使用 XLA 编译器栈。2020 年，Google 推出了首个面向 TPU 的 PyTorch 编译版本 PyTorch/XLA，基于 Lazy Tensors。尽管具有奠基意义，这一早期集成难以跟上 PyTorch 由社区驱动的快速演进。关键在于，PyTorch/XLA 需要侵入式修改源代码以显式定义可编译区域，编译时延迟严重，不支持 PyTorch 原生的命令式（“eager”）执行模式，并且在支持 PyTorch 生态内新兴的分布式计算原语方面滞后。与 PyTorch/XLA 和 TorchAX 等以往将 PyTorch 强行塞入 JAX 运作方式的尝试不同，TorchTPU 是作为 PyTorch 的一个符合设计原则的 TPU 后端而构建的：eager 执行是首要优先级，现有 PyTorch 工作负载只需极少的代码改动即可开箱即用（例如， .to("cuda") → .to("tpu") ）。
TorchTPU 正在积极开发中，它已在生产环境中用于部分最大 Google Cloud 客户的推理和训练工作负载，并且可以在该 GitHub 仓库 中找到其开源项目。撰写本文时，我们已：
在本文档的剩余部分，我们将讨论 TorchTPU 架构的关键方面以及一些初步结果。
Google TPU 是专门设计的 ASIC ，用于执行作为深度学习基础的巨量张量运算。从 硬件架构角度 来看，一个 TPU 芯片 包含（取决于代际）：
TPU 通过两个不同的入口点使用 XLA 编译器 栈进行编程： StableHLO （用于 ML 算子的较高级 IR）和 Mosaic （用于自定义内核的较低级 IR ）。实际的 TPU ISA 是专有的、可能发生变化且不公开。实际上，可以将 StableHLO 以及（更是如此）Mosaic 视为等同于 PTX。参见下图的高层示意图。
C++ 程序可以通过实例化 PjRT Client 来访问本地 TPU，其 API 提供了将 MLIR（StableHLO 或 Mosaic）编译为 TPU 可执行文件、启动该可执行文件以及在 TPU 之间复制数据的方法。请注意，TPU 执行是异步的，CPU 可以通过等待关联的 PjRTBuffer 来等待 TPU 结果就绪。
我们在设计 TorchTPU 时考虑了可用性。当用户在安装了 TorchTPU wheel 的 TPU 机器上导入 PyTorch 时，在 TPU 上运行 PyTorch 代码只需进行微不足道的更改，并且得益于 PyTorch 的自动加载机制，只需几行代码即可完成：
TorchTPU 为 TPU 硬件适配标准 PyTorch 精度 API。与所有高性能机器学习架构一样，TPU 针对其特定代际所偏好的原生数据类型进行了优化，以实现峰值性能和能效。对于 TPU，原生矩阵乘法格式为 bfloat16（BF16），它在高动态范围与高效吞吐之间取得平衡。由于 TPU 矩阵乘法单元（MXU）被设计为使用 BF16 输入执行算术运算，并以 32 位浮点进行中间累加，这一配置是 TPU 高性能计算的基石。对于非收缩运算（例如逐元素加法、激活、layernorm 和 softmax），TorchTPU 使用 TPU 向量执行单元（VPU）执行 FP32 张量运算，该单元原生执行完整的 IEEE-754 FP32 算术。
TorchTPU 将 PyTorch 精度模式映射到底层 XLA/StableHLO 配置，以暴露这一硬件能力：
对于绝大多数深度学习工作负载，我们建议使用 medium （默认）精度。在 TorchTPU 中显式选择 high 或 highest 会触发性能警告（ TORCH_WARN_ONCE ）。只有在明确识别到与精度相关的收敛问题时才切换到 high 或 highest ，因为这些模式会带来显著的性能开销。除全局设置外，TorchTPU 还提供线程本地上下文管理器（ torch.tpu.precision ）用于细粒度作用域（例如针对数值敏感的层）。
遵循 这份 PyTorch 指南 ，我们通过一个新的 C++ 后端扩展了 PyTorch dispatcher，并将其注册为 PrivateUse1 。此外，我们使用了标准的 at::Tensor 机制来定义张量存储的设备特定实现（通过在 c10::StorageImpl 内使用 c10::UniqueVoidPtr ）。

items.title: 编程 Agent 增长遭遇人类评审瓶颈：Tessl 博客解析信任赤字
items.description: Tessl 博客引用 Jellyfish 2026 年 9 月 AI Engineering Trends 数据指出，中位数公司已有 22% 的合并 PR 由自主编码 Agent 撰写（90 分位达 53%），但仅约 0.6% 的 PR 由 Agent 评审合并（前 10% 公司为 9%）。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/wz8yuzgpztob6gtdo8pxuip2j
items.excerpt:
There Aren’t Enough Chaperones for All Your Coding Agents
Tessl 博客引用 Jellyfish 2026 年 9 月 AI Engineering Trends 数据指出，中位数公司已有 22% 的合并 PR 由自主编码 Agent 撰写（90 分位达 53%），但仅约 0.6% 的 PR 由 Agent 评审合并（前 10% 公司为 9%）。
基于 Jellyfish 平台数据指出 agent 写码占比与人工评审瓶颈的落差，并归纳领先团队用平台工程加速建立信任的做法。
这些开发者足够可靠，你会让他们写代码，但他们需要相当多的监督。他们不能独自担任他人工作的审查者，当然也不能批准将代码合并到重要系统中。就开发者而言，他们属于二等公民。
传统软件工程会将这种状况视为严重的结构性问题。高效的开发团队建立在信任高自主性个体的基础之上——这些人（配合良好的流程和保障措施）能够编写、审查和交付代码，而无需被微观管理。
然而，这正是当今典型工程团队所处的境况，只不过我们所说的这 20% 开发者是 AI 智能体。大多数团队要求每个智能体都有人陪同——而陪同人员根本不够用。
在 Jellyfish，我们追踪工程组织如何使用 AI 编码工具和智能体，以及这种使用如何与产出相关联，比如实际交付了什么代码、构建了哪些产品和功能，以及这些事情的成 本是多少。通过我们的平台，我们可以洞察约 1,300 家公司中的约 30 万名工程师和超过 1 亿个拉取请求，这是业内最大的软件工程工作流数据集。
在最近一期的月度 AI 工程趋势报告 中，有两张图表尤其凸显了工程团队在扩大自主编码智能体使用规模时面临的挑战。
第一张是自主智能体活动，我们将其定义为一 家公司已合并 PR 中由自主编码智能体编写的比例（即由编码智能体编写代码、提交和/或发起 PR）。中位数公司目前为 22% 的 PR，高于一个月前的 18%。处于第 90 百分位的公司为 53%。
按公司百分位划分的自主智能体活动。来源：Jellyfish AI 工程趋势，2026 年 9 月。
对于任何在 2026 年使用过 AI 编码智能体的人来说，这些工具的惊人普及率应该不会太令人意外。执行框架和模型能力的进步使 AI 编码智能体能够接管很大一部分编码工作负载。但可以说，这只是“原始编码”部分——你仍然需要批准、合并和部署这些代码。
让我们看另一张图表：“智能体合并的 PR”，即由智能体审查并合并、未经人工审查的拉取请求。这种做法远不那么常见。中位数公司仅对约 0.6% 的 PR 实现了纯 AI 审查，而排名前 10% 的公司为 9% 且仍在攀升。
按公司百分位划分的智能体合并 PR。来源：Jellyfish AI 工程趋势，2026 年 9 月。
因此，在典型公司中，智能体现在编写了约五分之一的代码，但几乎所有这些代码在流程的某个环节都需要人工介入。这种人工监督是建立信任和确保质量的合理方式，但它也构成了编码智能体能够提供多少额外产能的硬性约束。
大家都在谈论软件工厂，但一个每个单元在出厂前都必须经过人工检验的工厂并不是工厂——它只是一个拥有更多传送带的工作坊。
评审瓶颈不仅让工程师们倍感压力，也让领导团队倍感压力，因为它是造成 ROI 问题的一大因素。
所谓“ROI 问题”，我指的是上游代码创建速度的提升远比下游影响更为显著。例如，在 2026 年全年，我们普遍测到拉取请求（PR）数量增长了约 2 倍，但已交付功能等产品产出仅增长了约 40-50%。
造成这一差距的原因之一是，由智能体编写的 PR 在早期阶段就失败的比例要高得多。当由人类编写 PR 时，约有 20% 的情况无法合并，原因各种各样且完全正常（例如实验性工作、方案错误、新需求、优先级变化）。而对于智能体，放弃率翻了一倍（40% 对 20%）。与此同时，那些确实合并了的智能体 PR 反而受到更多审查而非更少：过去一年里，每个已合并智能体 PR 所获得的人工评审数量增加了一倍多。
这些本身都并非不合理。智能体代码确实更难评审，评审者对其保持谨慎是正确的。问题在于，随着编码智能体能力持续增长，这些负担给整个系统带来的压力。评审负担随着智能体产出的增加而扩大，而人类注意力始终是固定的约束，并且我上面展示的自主性曲线每个月都在复利式增长。
如果今天处于中位水平的公司达到今天前 10% 公司的水平（即自主智能体编写超过一半的代码），代码评审就有可能变成人类的全部工作，从而挤占经验丰富的开发者本应从事的其他所有重要事项的时间，比如与产品和设计协作、塑造软件架构，以及将他们的工程判断力用于那些没有明确解决方案的问题。
幸运的是，一些公司正在解决这个问题。那些让自主智能体合并 9% PR 的顶尖公司，并不是在盲目地更加信任它们的智能体。相反，它们投入精力来加速信任的建立速度。
这通常涉及大量平台工作，例如将低风险工作路由给自主智能体的系统、用于安全可靠开发与部署的沙箱和预发布环境，当然还有大量的自动化测试。不过，也许最重要的是，它们很早就开始并大力推进；信任只能随时间建立，你等待得越久，就要越久地忍受不断堆积的评审积压。
如果你有兴趣进一步了解自主智能体如何演进（或者更准确地说，如何颠覆）SDLC，欢迎于 11 月 2 日至 4 日在纽约市参加 aiDevCon 。我将在我的演讲 《Botsitting Doesn’t Scale: How to Navigate the Autonomy-Trust Gridlock in Real Engineering Orgs》 中谈论这一点以及更多内容，并分享我们从分析 Jellyfish 数据中学到的内容：最优秀的工程团队如何应对 2026 年最大的工程工作流挑战。
基于 Jellyfish 平台数据指出 agent 写码占比与人工评审瓶颈的落差，并归纳领先团队用平台工程加速建立信任的做法。

items.title: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts)
items.description: My new book is out today... what happened since the last one
items.excerpt:
My second book on AI, Co-Existence, is out today (and you can get it here ), 30 months after the release of Co-Intelligence in early 2024. Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts.
Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. In the current era of agentic AI that I cover in Co-Existence , I delegated the work and let the AI handle it. In this case, I used Opus 5.5 in Claude Projects, which allows you to talk to a single “orchestrator” agent that then spins off additional agents as needed, giving them instructions and relaying information back to you. Getting the work done was straightforward. I gave the AI a couple sentences of suggestions and it did what would have taken me hours of work (all the research, all the graphing, all the layouts, all the images, all the citations…) in minutes. And since I didn’t have to do the work, I had the AI make many options for me. I picked some and gave handwavy reactions to others that would drive a human team mad (“make it better”). It even caught that I’d gotten the math wrong. I was going to call this post “28 months on the exponential.”
I wrote this in my last book on AI, and it has continued to be literally true at every moment since. From early 2023 through early 2024, there was a single AI model that was undeniably the best in the world: GPT-4 from OpenAI. This was the AI model that most people remember from the first couple years of AI use, it was the one I thought about while writing Co-Intelligence , and it was the one that gave ChatGPT its status as the default AI for many people. Since then, twenty different AI models have held the lead at one time or another, all from Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI.
But the changing lead alone hides an even bigger change. A total of 180 AI models are now better than GPT-4 was at its release, many of which are open weights models, which anyone is free to use or modify. Nineteen of them can run on a modern smartphone.

items.title: ALTK-Evolve: How learned memory tops the τ²-bench leaderboard on customer service tasks without a frontier model
items.excerpt:
ALTK-Evolve learns and applies a playbook using GPT-4.1, outperforming the retail entries on τ²-bench, a customer service agent benchmark—without updating model weights.
Using GPT-4.1, an older, non-reasoning model, a basic customer-service agent reaches 67.5% Pass^4 on τ²-bench retail — meaning it solves the task on all four independent attempts for 67.5% of tasks. It scores above every retail entry in our October 12, 2026 leaderboard snapshot. It runs on the benchmark's stock ReAct scaffold, with learned guidelines appended to its system prompt.
ALTK-Evolve builds that playbook using GPT-4.1. It analyzes the agent's training-task attempts and uses the model to distill successes and failures into short behavioral rules: how to authenticate a customer, confirm a transaction, or handle a return. Those guidelines are then added to the agent's prompt for subsequent conversations. The same model powers both guideline extraction and the agent; no weight updates or human annotation are needed.
Our previous work demonstrated this approach on coding agents. Here, we test it on customer service, where success requires following domain policies, understanding a customer's request, and executing the right tool actions.
τ²-bench (from Sierra) measures how well an agent handles customer-service conversations under real constraints. Each task pairs the agent with an LLM-simulated customer who has a goal in mind, a set of domain tools (look up an order, issue a refund, rebook a flight), and a written policy document the agent must follow. The agent has to draw out the right details, stay within policy, and take the correct — often irreversible — actions; a task counts as solved only when the final database state matches the expected outcome, a strict binary reward. We use its two customer-service domains, retail and airline .
We run τ²-bench's own implementation of a basic ReAct agent with a two-phase THINK → ACT loop, using gpt-4.1 as the agent model and gpt-5.5 as the customer-simulator model; 4 trials per task. The only change we make is a block of learned guidelines appended to the system prompt — everything else (policy, tools, scaffold) is stock τ²-bench. Concretely, the learned guidelines are tacked on after the domain policy as a plain markdown list:
We extract guidelines from the agent's trajectories on τ²-bench train tasks using gpt-4.1 , the same model that powers the agent, then apply them unchanged on the held-out test set.

items.excerpt:
When a breaker keeps tripping every time the toaster and microwave run together, most people react the same way. They search online and call the first company that looks trustworthy.
That company often promises to handle everything: panel upgrades, furnace tune-ups, drain cleaning. However, an expert, like San Jose electrical contractor Fuse Service , is required for an electrical issue, not just the first result that comes up in a search.
Most homeowners lump plumbers, HVAC techs, and electricians together as “the people who come fix the house”. But electrical work runs on its own licensing system. Furthermore, it’s not usually a licensed electrician who comes to fix your wiring. It makes a difference.
Ask three homeowners what electrical contracting is, and you’ll hear three answers. Most will say it’s just “electrician work”. Close, but not quite.
An electrician is a licensed individual. A contractor is a licensed business. They carry liability insurance and workers’ comp if they have employees. In many states, they also have a bond. Plus, they can pull permits in your city.
Electrical contracting covers business tasks like estimates, permits, ordering, and staffing. It also involves getting approval from the inspector when they arrive. The electrician does the wiring. The company is responsible for whether that wiring is legal.
Plenty of small outfits are one person wearing both hats. In bigger shops, the license holder might never see your drywall.
Residential work breaks into a few buckets that don’t resemble each other on price. Service and repair is the bread and butter: dead outlets, flickering lights, a breaker that won’t stay set, a bathroom GFCI that trips when it rains. One tech, usually under two hours.
Upgrade work is the next tier. Panel replacements, a 240-volt line for an EV charger or a range, new circuits for a kitchen wired in 1974 for a toaster and a radio. Permits almost always apply.
Rough-in and new construction involve different challenges than additions or garage conversions. Total house rewires often happen alongside other crews. Their deadlines don’t change for anyone else’s needs.
Then there’s the challenge of the specialty work in new construction. Generators, pool equipment, surge protectors, and landscape lights all add up. Not every shop does all of it; it’s worth asking before anyone drives out.

items.title: Nuclear-Powered Car Carriers Face a Reality Test
items.description: Hyundai Glovis and Liberty Global Logistics are studying nuclear-powered car carriers, but commercial approval, port access and costs remain unanswered. The post Nuclear-Powered Car Carriers Face a Reality Test appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A nuclear-powered car carrier traveling between South Korea and the United States sounds like a concept from the distant future. Two logistics companies have now begun a practical examination of what would be required to operate one commercially. The distinction between studying the idea and ordering a ship is essential.
Hyundai Glovis and U.S.-based Liberty Global Logistics announced a memorandum of understanding in early October to evaluate a pure car and truck carrier powered by a small modular reactor, or SMR. The initial concept is potential service between South Korea and the United States, with regulatory feasibility work focused initially on U.S. West Coast ports. Their work will examine commercial viability, regulatory approvals, vessel construction, ports, and operating requirements.
Hyundai Glovis had previously received Approval in Principle from Lloyd's Register for its nuclear-powered car carrier concept in June. That is a meaningful design-review milestone, but it is not permission to build, fuel, or operate a nuclear merchant vessel.
Ocean shipping remains heavily dependent on conventional marine fuels. Operators face pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while navigating uncertain fuel costs, evolving regulations, and uneven availability of lower-carbon alternatives.
Nuclear propulsion offers an unusual theoretical advantage: a vessel could travel for extended periods without conventional fuel bunkering or carbon emissions from onboard fuel combustion. Long-range vehicle carriers might benefit from reduced bunker dependence and greater freedom from fuel-supply constraints.
The value proposition is more complex than the fuel bill, however. Reactor procurement, shielding, safety systems, maintenance, specialized crews, decommissioning, and financing would need to be included in a full lifecycle assessment. It is not yet clear what these costs would look like for a commercially operated car carrier.
The nuclear option also introduces risks that conventional ships do not face, including radiation protection, security, emergency response, and specialized infrastructure obligations. A technically feasible vessel may still be commercially impractical.
A merchant ship cannot operate on an ocean route without access to suitable ports. Liberty Global Logistics will evaluate the U.S. regulatory and operational environment, initially concentrating on West Coast ports. Hyundai Glovis will examine the corresponding Korean requirements.

items.title: Investing in Eka Robotics
items.description: a16z leads Eka Robotics’ Series A
items.excerpt:
The human hand may be the most economically important machine ever built.
Much of the world’s physical economy—from manufacturing and electronics assembly to logistics and food production—still depends on people using their hands. Industrial robots have transformed highly structured production, where fixtures hold every part in place and robots repeat the same motion quickly and precisely.
But enormous categories of physical work remain hard to automate, because the real world is variable. Parts move. Materials deform. Objects slip. Connectors don’t align perfectly.
That creates an enormous economic opportunity. If robots can reliably perform the dexterous tasks people do every day, automation can expand beyond repetitive, engineered processes into a much larger share of physical work. Labor is already a constraint across many of these industries, and the value of a machine that combines human versatility with machine speed, reliability and uptime is difficult to overstate.
We believe solving dexterous manipulation is one of the largest opportunities in robotics. It’s why we’re excited to lead the Series A in Eka Robotics .
Modern AI is making extraordinary progress in helping robots understand what to do . Vision models can recognize objects and estimate their position. Language models can interpret instructions and reason about complex topics. World models can increasingly reason about scenes and plan actions.
But knowing what should happen isn’t the same as physically making it happen.
Consider inserting a connector. Vision can tell a robot where the socket is. But once contact begins, the important information changes. Has one edge caught? Is the connector beginning to bind? Should the robot push harder, rotate slightly, or pull back?
Humans answer these questions almost effortlessly through our sense of touch.
The human hand has roughly two dozen degrees of freedom, but mechanics are only part of what makes it remarkable. Our fingertips and palms contain thousands of specialized sensory receptors . Some detect sustained pressure and shape; others detect light touch and the first signs of slip, high-frequency vibration, or the stretching of our skin. Combined with proprioception from our muscles and joints, they give the brain a remarkably rich, continuous picture of what is happening at the point of contact.
That is why you can pick up an egg without crushing it, tighten your grip on a glass the instant it starts to slip, or find the thread of a screw

items.title: Vention launches 24/7 video-based remote support
items.description: Building on the Remote Support service it introduced in 2023, Vention now connects manufacturers with automation experts on every shift. The post Vention launches 24/7 video-based remote support appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Vention has launched round-the-clock, video-based remote support, giving manufacturers live access to Vention automation experts at any hour of any day. The company is demonstrating the service this week at PACK EXPO International in Chicago alongside the Rapid Series Palletizer 3.0 and its connected conveyor ecosystem.
Building on the Remote Support service it introduced in 2023, Vention now connects manufacturers with automation experts on every shift. When a line stops at 2:00 a.m., the operator can open a live video session from the machine pendant and reach an expert within 10 minutes. The expert joins with the full context of the machine, including hardware and firmware versions, real-time I/O state, and the program running on MachineMotion AI .
“Our customers now have two kinds of expertise working for them at any hour,” said Etienne Lacroix, founder and CEO of Vention. “Vention’s automation experts are available on every shift, and AI agents like MachineAgent help their teams understand and improve performance across every line. Together, they keep production moving long after installation.”
Founded in 2016, Vention offers an AI -powered, full-stack platform that unifies hardware, software, and physical AI into one experience. The Montreal-based company has over 28,000 machines deployed worldwide, in a community of more than 6,000 factories.
With remote support, the pendant’s front and back cameras give the expert a clear view of the cell, while human-machine interface ( HMI ) screen sharing, voice, and chat keep the operator and expert working side by side. For deeper troubleshooting, the operator can grant the expert remote access to the pendant, allowing them to adjust or update the machine’s code directly.
Vention’s support team guides the operator through each step and assigns the right resources to every request, resolving 90% of issues remotely. When on-site presence is needed, more than 40 Vention field experts are ready to deploy, keeping production running at the pace operations demand.
MachineAnalytics is now available directly on the pendant, and every palletizer ships with a pre-built palletizing dashboard tracking boxes per minute, OEE, uptime, and other key metrics from day one. The dashboard shows what caused a stop and what could cause the next one, while RemoteView gives plant and engineering teams the same live visibility from anywhere.
MachineAgent takes this further, allowing teams to build their own MachineAnalytics templates

items.title: Locus Robotics finds Gen Z shoppers are four times more likely than boomers to plan to return purchases
items.description: 'Bracketing' among younger apparel shoppers is one of several generational buying habits leading to more returns, found Locus. The post Locus Robotics finds Gen Z shoppers are four times more likely than boomers to plan to return purchases appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Younger shoppers are reshaping purchasing and returns behaviors across apparel, beauty, and skincare in ways that are creating fulfillment requirements that automation can address, found Locus Robotics Corp. The company today released research noting that 61% of Gen Z apparel shoppers “bracket” their purchases, buying multiple sizes or styles to keep just one, compared with only 15% of baby boomers.
Younger shoppers are also far more likely to discover products through social media and make purchases quickly after discovery, said Locus. For retailers in these categories, those generational behaviors reinforce the need for flexible automation systems that can adapt as volume, order profiles, and channels change.
“Retail fulfillment operators are facing an entirely new reality, where demand patterns can change in hours and days, not seasons,” said Rick Faulk, CEO of Locus Robotics. “We’re seeing this firsthand with a record number of peak robot requests to help retailers around the world respond to demand surges. The generational shifts underscore why warehouses need automation that can flex with volume, adapt across workflows, and evolve as consumer behavior and business needs continue to evolve.”
Locus Robotics claimed that it is a leader in “ Flexibility-First Warehouse Automation ,” helping enterprises perform in an uncertain world. Powered by the LocusONE platform, the Wilmington, Mass.-based company combines real-time orchestration, advanced robotics, and AI -driven execution to automate fulfillment operations at scale.
Bracketing is generational, and for many it’s a habit: Sixty-one percent of Gen Z and 52% of millennials have bracketed an apparel purchase, compared with 37% of Gen X and just 15% of baby boomers, creating additional returns volume that retailers must absorb without slowing or disrupting order fulfillment.
Social discovery makes timing harder to predict: Seventy-nine percent of Gen Z shoppers and 75% of millennials have bought an apparel , beauty, or skincare product after discovering it on social media , compared with 26% of baby boomers. More than two-thirds of those buyers purchased within three days, creating the potential for sudden demand spikes as trends take off almost overnight.
Availability depends on keeping inventory moving: Thirty-three percent of shoppers said an unavailable item, size, shade, or formula led them to abandon or delay a purchase, the most frequently cited reason, while 17% require same- or next-day delivery

items.title: 美国陆军网络司令部 ECHOTRIBBLE 项目拟将 AI 智能体变成自主扩散的网络武器
items.description: 据 The Intercept 获取的文件，美国陆军网络司令部（ARCYBER）正在开发代号 ECHOTRIBBLE 的平台，让 AI 智能体自主在网络间移动、识别并清除威胁目标，之后自毁，且须在极少人工监督下运行。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/u6kqfrgiqrhbpxn012nlisd66
items.excerpt:
Army Cyber Command's ECHOTRIBBLE would turn AI agents into self-spreading cyberweapons
据 The Intercept 获取的文件，美国陆军网络司令部（ARCYBER）正在开发代号 ECHOTRIBBLE 的平台，让 AI 智能体自主在网络间移动、识别并清除威胁目标，之后自毁，且须在极少人工监督下运行。
文件披露 ARCYBER 让 AI 智能体自主扩散和清除目标的计划，多位安全研究者指出了误伤和失控风险。
内部文件显示，陆军网络司令部正在构建能够自行穿越其他网络并“清除”目标的AI代理。专家警告称，附带损害将几乎无法控制。
据 The Intercept 获得的文件显示，陆军网络司令部（ARCYBER）正在开发一个旨在将AI代理转变为自主武器的平台。一份面向潜在承包商的文件称，该程序代号为“ECHOTRIBBLE”，“旨在自主导航基础设施”。它应具备“识别并清除已识别威胁/目标”的能力。
目前，ARCYBER的进攻性黑客行动大多由坐在电脑前的士兵执行。一份面向有意向供应商的问答文件明确指出，ECHOTRIBBLE“主要聚焦于”攻击。根据该文件，清除目标可能意味着“完全或暂时使威胁失效，从目标中删除威胁”。
该系统应像计算机蠕虫一样运作，在设备之间未被察觉地跳转，直到找到目标。这既要在云环境中奏效，也要在无网络连接的“气隙”系统上奏效。任务完成后，代理应自我销毁。陆军可以在开始时设置“预定义触发器”，但该软件“必须在极少人工监督下运行”，并具备“自主导向行为”能力。
The Intercept报道称，该项目仍处于早期阶段。在 6月24日ARCYBER活动 上面向潜在供应商的演示展示了它可能的样子。一旦该软件进入笔记本电脑，它就会“识别”同一网络上的“其他潜在目标”，并“生成一个专门为iPad、Apple台式机和Windows 11 PC定制的自身副本”。
过去几个月里，OpenAI及其他公司测试中的代理多次无意中闯入外部系统及其开发者自己的系统。目标包括 RubyGems 、 Hugging Face 以及澳大利亚政府的 Medicare统计门户 。代理还曾试图闯入美国教育部。在这些案例中，它们都没有被指示发动攻击。
蒙特利尔大学机器学习教授David Krueger表示，已观察到AI系统在知情的情况下攻击甚至并非其目标的系统。他说，鉴于这些已知的故障模式，命令自主系统“清除”威胁“极其危险”。
AI安全公司Abundant的CEO Hyrum Anderson也警告了在抵达目标途中可能造成的损害。例如，如果对手将其指挥基础设施设在一家美国水务公司，代理可能会攻击那里。他说，处于“安全贫困线”以下的组织——从牙科诊所到关键基础设施——面临的风险最大。在压力下，代理往往将护栏视为障碍，而一旦命令是“摧毁”，爆炸半径可能会急剧扩大。
兰德公司的William Marcellino指出，这些系统缺乏判断力。他说，人们之所以信任一名配备实弹的19岁海军陆战队员，是因为他对世界有足够的了解，能够识别出自己不该做什么。而当今公开可用的AI并不具备这种能力。

items.excerpt:
Web applications have become an integral part of how industrial companies track their daily operations. Instead of dealing with service requests alone or routinely tracking supply chains or equipment records, companies rely on management software to take that burden off the staff.
However, industrial web applications are just as vulnerable to cyberattacks as most other apps. A weak login, exposed API, or a broken access rule can all become a quick entry point for an attacker trying to get access to sensitive data.
Add to this the speed at which new updates or features are usually rolled out, and the risk of sensitive data exposure increases tenfold. This is why most industrial companies are turning to AI-powered penetration testing tools, which help speed up security testing and enable teams to hunt for vulnerabilities live.
If you’re looking for an AI pentesting tool and don’t want to spend hours on demo calls just to find out that the tool you picked is not suitable for your situation, you’re in the right place. items.title: llm-d 1.0 发布：Kubernetes 原生分布式推理服务走向生产就绪
items.description: IBM、Red Hat 和 Google 等主导的开源推理项目 llm-d 在 PyTorch Conference North America 上发布 llm-d 1.0，这是一个 Kubernetes 原生的分布式推理服务框架，支持任意模型、任意加速器和任意云。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/b1pcaa7ceghor24vjgsjagqqd
items.excerpt:
llm-d 1.0 hardens open-source AI inference for production
IBM、Red Hat 和 Google 等主导的开源推理项目 llm-d 在 PyTorch Conference North America 上发布 llm-d 1.0，这是一个 Kubernetes 原生的分布式推理服务框架，支持任意模型、任意加速器和任意云。
原文给出 llm-d 1.0 的具体能力变化和实测成本数据，读者可据此评估自建推理基础设施是否划算。
今天在北美 PyTorch 大会上，llm-d 项目贡献者宣布推出 llm-d 1.0，这是开源 AI 基础设施的一个重要里程碑。作为一个 Kubernetes 原生的 分布式推理服务网络 ，llm-d 使得在任何云上、任何加速器上为任何模型部署推理栈成为可能。
此次发布标志着 llm-d 已不再局限于展示单项性能技术，而是准备好支撑生产环境的现实需求：在多种工作负载下保持持续效率，同时在需求不断增长的情况下平衡各项服务优先级。随着推理成本上升，llm-d 旨在帮助企业将模型部署引入内部，并让 AI 投资获得回报。
这项工作由一个不断壮大的开源社区共同开发，成员包括硬件提供商、模型开发者、云平台和企业用户。作为 llm-d 的首席维护者，Red Hat、IBM 和 Google 帮助将先进的推理技术转化为企业可规模化运营的协同系统。这三家公司去年与 CoreWeave 和 NVIDIA 共同创立了 llm-d，AMD、Cisco、Hugging Face、Intel、Lambda 和 Mistral AI 等行业领导者也陆续作为贡献者加入。
其成果是为那些希望获得前沿级推理性能、又不想完全依赖某一家专有模型提供商、云或硬件平台的组织，提供了一个厂商中立的替代方案。
“llm-d 已为第 2 天运维做好准备，”IBM Research 杰出工程师、llm-d 联合创始人兼首席维护者 Carlos Costa 表示。“llm-d 一直在为生产工作负载提供最先进的推理性能。1.0 带来的是成熟度，使其能像任何其他关键服务一样运行：稳定的 API、多个优先级相互竞争的租户共享同一基础设施，以及不中断业务的升级。这正是我们构建 llm-d 1.0 的目的。”
自 llm-d 发布以来，项目一直聚焦于改进 AI 推理的五种重要方法：前缀缓存感知路由，将请求导向可能已持有其共享上下文的基础设施；KV 缓存卸载，通过在 GPU、CPU 和存储资源之间移动缓存信息来延长其有效寿命；批推理优化，将工作分组以便基础设施更高效地处理；预填充/解码分离，将读取提示词的工作与生成响应的工作分开；以及宽专家并行，将大型混合专家模型分布到众多加速器上。
在 1.0 版本中，llm-d 已成熟为一个能够支持第 2 天运维的栈：即 AI 服务部署之后必须发生的一切。这包括服务具有竞争优先级的工作负载、管理不同的性能需求、保持效率、优先处理重要服务，以及让系统长期保持可靠。基准测试可以表明某项功能提升了吞吐量，但生产系统必须在流量变化、硬件故障、软件更新或不同用户争夺同一资源时仍持续提供这种性能。llm-d 1.0 的目标就是让各项技术在这些更不可预测的条件下协同工作。
llm-d 1.0 在已经让 llm-d 成为强大分布式推理工具的核心技术创新基础上进一步扩展，增强了对多租户服务质量、零停机运维和智能体感知服务的支持，以在常见的第 2 天生产运维中保持持续性能。企业 AI 服务可能通过同一端点接收来自人员和自主智能体的请求，但这些工作负载的行为方式不同。使用编码助手的人期望快速得到答案。智能体可能发送大量突发请求，在使用工具时暂停，然后返回进行下一轮模型调用。
借助 流控 ，llm-d 1.0 可以管理工作负载是共享同一硬件还是跨越多种加速器时的竞争优先级。流控、公平性和优先级排序有助于防止突发工作负载压垮对延迟敏感的服务。在需求很高时，系统可以更审慎地决定哪些请求应优先获得资源。请求还可以在多个轮次中保持绑定到适当的基础设施。这可以保持其前缀缓存处于热状态，提高先前处理过的上下文被复用而不是重新计算的机会。
这对对话式助手很重要，但对智能体尤其有价值。智能体在执行任务时经常回到相同的代码、文档、指令和对话历史。前缀缓存感知路由会将每一轮发送到已经持有相关上下文的副本，而 KV 缓存卸载有助于在 GPU 内存受限时保留更多可复用信息。这就是生产就绪在实践中的样子：通过理解到达模型的工作并相应地管理基础设施，更有效、更具成本效益地提供模型服务。
这种对生产的关注直接关系到 AI 的经济性。随着 AI 进入日常业务运营，推理已成为一项经常性支出。智能体系统可能会增加这项支出，因为单个任务可能涉及多轮推理、工具使用、评估和修订。如果每一步都需要模型重新阅读相同材料，你就是在为系统已经完成的工作反复付费。
在最近一次智能体编码工作负载测试中，llm-d 的前缀感知路由器捕获了 97% 的可用缓存复用 。通过避免重复计算并更高效地利用现有硬件，这类技术可以降低大规模提供 AI 服务的成本。在另一项近期演示中，IBM 和 Red Hat 在自托管部署上同时运行了 3,000 个软件工程智能体，成本比以服务形式提供同一开放模型的实际价格 低 5 到 10 倍 。
当组织运营自己的基础设施时，基础设施就成为可管理的成本结构的一部分。通过将开放权重模型与开放服务栈相结合，llm-d 为组织提供了另一种选择，用以控制 AI 使用量、基础设施支出和业务价值之间的关系。
llm-d 可与 vLLM 或 SGLang 等推理引擎配合使用，增加将模型服务器转变为生产服务所需的分布式路由和运维能力。
这也让 llm-d 在更广泛的开源生态系统中扮演了重要角色。PyTorch 与开发 AI 模型和应用的人群密切相关。而作为沙箱项目 托管 llm-d 的云原生计算基金会（CNCF），则更侧重于在生

items.title: How AI Confidentiality Gaps Are Becoming a Liability for Robotics Firms
items.description: It often feels like the more deadlines compress and documentation piles stack up, the longer code reviews take. These days, demand is stronger than ever, and the expectation that you can do it faster than ever means that the promise of AI assistance sitting right there in a browser tab is hard to resist. The […]
items.excerpt:
It often feels like the more deadlines compress and documentation piles stack up, the longer code reviews take. These days, demand is stronger than ever, and the expectation that you can do it faster than ever means that the promise of AI assistance sitting right there in a browser tab is hard to resist.
The problem is that “right there in a browser tab” usually means ChatGPT, and ChatGPT means OpenAI’s servers, and OpenAI’s servers means your proprietary motion control algorithms or your client’s confidential information is no longer entirely yours.
In 2023, Samsung engineers made headlines after accidentally leaking confidential semiconductor code and internal meeting transcripts by pasting them directly into ChatGPT. Samsung responded by banning the tool internally. Most robotics firms haven’t had their moment yet, and some haven’t learned from the tech giant’s mistakes.
Density of the day to day workload is the biggest problem. Debugging, drafting client integration specs, summarising months of competitive research, pulling together documentation from internal test results. All of them have obvious reasons to reach for an AI assistant, and all of them are working with information that would be genuinely damaging in the wrong hands.
Besides, AI is changing client expectations of what a “fast turnaround” really is.
OpenAI’s terms of service state that prompts can be used to improve their models unless users actively opt out through enterprise settings, which is something that many employees on free or standard accounts simply don’t have access to. The gap between “the policy exists” and “the team knows about it and has configured it correctly” is where most of the exposure happens.
Passing client data through a consumer AI product without explicit authorisation can constitute a breach of contract or a violation of NDA terms that the firm signed before the project started.
There’s also the sector-specific angle. Companies building robots for healthcare or critical infrastructure are subject to data regulations that apply regardless of whether the data leakage was intentional. “An engineer used a free chatbot” is not a defence that tends to go particularly far.
The exposure tends to be invisible right up until it isn’t. No alert goes off when an engineer pastes a wiring schematic into a chatbot. The firm finds out when the client finds out, or when a competitor’s product looks remarkably familiar.

items.title: What Are the Most Common Mistakes Sales Teams Make When Using B2B Lead Generation Tools on LinkedIn?
items.description: The problem of unsuccessful LinkedIn lead generation is often not with the technology being used but rather with a decent technology used poorly. LinkedIn has managed to automate things to the point where even an average sales team is able to work with it on a large scale, but large-scale use of poor tactics grows […]
items.excerpt:
The problem of unsuccessful LinkedIn lead generation is often not with the technology being used but rather with a decent technology used poorly.
LinkedIn has managed to automate things to the point where even an average sales team is able to work with it on a large scale, but large-scale use of poor tactics grows faster than good ones.
LinkedIn promotes relevancy and penalizes quantity masquerading as engagement. Those teams that use LinkedIn as a numbers game, the idea being that more connections equal more messages equal more touches, will likely notice that the rate of acceptances and replies drops as they become more active, because both the system’s built-in detection technology and the users themselves are attuned to anything that appears automated and cookie-cutter.
But the underlying issue is often that the sales team adopts the tool first and then defines what “quality” looks like for their unique buyer.
Every automation tool does not suit every team’s risk appetite and process; moreover, choosing a tool by considering factors like cost and speed will lead to failure.
An automation tool that operates in the cloud and offers LinkedIn credentials to a third-party server is very different from an automation tool that operates from the user’s system or VPS and performs like a human being.
Another mistake many teams make is choosing a tool first without deciding on the strategy, where an aggressive connection-requesting tool used in a bad targeting strategy leads only to rejection.
A list based solely on the job title will generally be incorrect far more often than it is correct, since there is a varying level of influence that the same title may hold within different organizations.
There is also the issue that many teams are not using the targeted methods that are available to them, such as the use of the more advanced filters, the signals of recent career changes and “posted on LinkedIn”, all of which can be found through Sales Navigator but are overlooked for generic searches. The outcome is that there is much reach but very little target reached.
Another very common mistake in the use of LinkedIn outreach is sending in large volumes and without any personalization, but this is well justified by statistics, since according to scientific studies of B2B buyers’ behavior, the great majority of users just ignore all messages that have the appearance of mass mailings, whereas the acceptance rate and the number of replies are significantly higher for per

items.excerpt:
A field engineer can arrive with the right tools and still lack something essential: permission to open the information or system needed for the job.
A public manual, an internal service ticket and a machine interface may sit on the same laptop screen, yet each can require a different access arrangement.
Preparing those arrangements before departure makes the visit easier to manage. It also gives the engineer and site contact a shared answer when a connection fails. The useful question is specific: what must be opened, on which device, with whose approval, during this visit?
Start with the agreed work, then identify the resources needed to carry it out. For a hypothetical inspection visit, that might include a public maintenance manual, an internal job record and a supervised view of machine diagnostics. Listing them separately exposes dependencies that a general request for “internet access” can hide.
Public documentation usually needs an ordinary internet connection or an approved offline copy. An internal job record may require an employer-managed device and company sign-in.
Access to operational technology, or OT, depends on the site owner’s arrangements for systems that monitor or control physical processes.
Put an owner beside each resource. The person who approves access to a service ticket may have no authority to approve a machine session. Resolve that distinction before it becomes a conversation at the factory gate.
Keep the record proportionate to the visit. A short note naming the resource, approved device, access method and responsible contact may be enough. Store credentials through the approved system rather than placing them alongside the travel itinerary.
Check the model and version details needed to select the right documentation. A downloaded manual is useful only if it applies to the equipment and work in scope. Where the information is available, note the document version and the person who confirmed it.
Ask which material may be held offline. Public product documentation and customer drawings have different sharing conditions. Permission to read a drawing through a controlled portal does not automatically include permission to download it onto a personal laptop.
For approved offline material, use the storage method your organization requires. Confirm that the file opens before leaving and that any required viewing software is available. An offline copy that depends on an unavailable sign-in or missing application may offer little help

items.title: Select Technology for the System, Not the Feature List
items.description: Logistics software evaluations are still too often conducted as feature contests. That approach made more sense when applications were relatively self-contained. It makes much less sense when every important platform now sits inside a web of data, decisions, workflows, automation, and AI. The post Select Technology for the System, Not the Feature List appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Logistics software evaluations are still too often conducted as feature contests. That approach made more sense when applications were relatively self-contained. It makes much less sense when every important platform now sits inside a web of data, decisions, workflows, automation, and AI.
The traditional feature checklist is not enough. Technology selection increasingly needs a systems engineering lens. The earlier WMS architecture discussion illustrates the principle: feature breadth can be less important than how coherently a platform fits the operating system around it.
The first question should not be which product has the most functionality. It should be what role the technology is expected to play in the operating system.
Is the objective to reduce tender or exception latency? Improve customer-promise reliability? Automate repetitive routing and dispatch decisions? Increase warehouse throughput? Create a common decision layer across TMS, WMS, YMS, parcel, and visibility applications? Support a new fulfillment or delivery model?
The answer defines the mission. From there, the organization can translate the mission into requirements and evaluate technologies against them. This keeps the process centered on operational outcomes rather than vendor categories.
That distinction matters because product boundaries are blurring. TMS vendors are adding visibility, orchestration, and intelligence. WMS vendors are extending into labor, automation, and decision support. Visibility platforms are adding workflows and execution. Integration platforms are adding orchestration. AI is being embedded across nearly every logistics layer.
The category label tells you less than it once did.
A technology can be excellent in isolation and still be a poor fit for the system around it. Systems engineering pays close attention to interfaces for exactly this reason.
What data does the platform need? What events does it produce? How does it connect to existing systems? Can it support the required latency? How does it handle failures? What happens when an integration is unavailable? How portable are the data? How difficult is it to change surrounding components later?
These questions are often treated as IT due diligence after the functional evaluation. They should be part of the core selection process.

items.title: Why Mine Ventilation Fans Belong in the Automation Plan
items.description: A fan can be running normally while too little air reaches the working face. An extended duct run or a leaking connection may be enough to cause a shortfall, even when the motor shows no sign of trouble. Operators need to know how much air reaches each working area as well as whether the fan […]
items.excerpt:
A fan can be running normally while too little air reaches the working face. An extended duct run or a leaking connection may be enough to cause a shortfall, even when the motor shows no sign of trouble.
Operators need to know how much air reaches each working area as well as whether the fan is running. As mines introduce remote-controlled loaders and more automated production, fan selection and ventilation control need to be planned together.
Workers positioning an axial ventilation fan in an underground roadway.
Underground layouts rarely stay the same for long. Headings advance, ducts are extended and new connections alter the paths available to the air. A ventilation arrangement that worked earlier in a project may need adjustment as development continues.
Main fans provide the pressure that drives air through the principal ventilation circuit. Auxiliary fans and ducting serve blind headings and other areas that need local ventilation. Auxiliary ventilation depends on the main circuit for a sufficient fresh-air supply and a return path for contaminated air.
Reading a fan curve is easier when the duct system is considered alongside it. The operating point is where the pressure available from the fan matches the pressure needed to move air through that system.
Add duct length or a restrictive bend and the operating point can shift, even at an unchanged speed. That is why a catalogue airflow figure needs a stated pressure condition.
For a development heading using forcing ventilation, the specification should distinguish the air required at the duct outlet from the quantity entering the duct. Leakage means those figures may differ.
A supplier can then assess the complete duty instead of treating the largest catalogue airflow as the selection target. Check the longest planned duct run before equipment is ordered.
When comparing mine ventilation fans , the starting point is the required airflow and the pressure needed to deliver it through the planned system. State whether the pressure is static or total, and use performance data that account for the expected site air density.
The motor’s kilowatt rating cannot answer the selection question on its own. Fans with the same motor power can have quite different airflow and pressure characteristics.
If a project calls for variable speed control, the fan needs to suit the range of duties it will encounter. It must meet the design duty and remain stable and efficient at the lower airflow and pressure combinations

items.title: Upgrade Your Golf Cart Performance With the Right Battery Choice
items.description: Golf carts have evolved far beyond the fairway. They shuttle families through retirement communities, haul equipment across commercial properties, and navigate sprawling resorts from dawn until well after dark. This expanded use places new demands on power systems originally designed for eighteen holes at a leisurely pace. A battery that barely completes a round under […]
items.excerpt:
Golf carts have evolved far beyond the fairway. They shuttle families through retirement communities, haul equipment across commercial properties, and navigate sprawling resorts from dawn until well after dark. This expanded use places new demands on power systems originally designed for eighteen holes at a leisurely pace.
A battery that barely completes a round under light use fails halfway through a busy day of errands, maintenance work, or transportation duty. The gap between adequate and exceptional performance often comes down to one component: the battery bank underneath the seat.
This guide shows golf course fleet managers, community residents, and commercial operators how the right battery upgrade transforms cart performance, lowers operating costs, and eliminates the frustration of dead carts stranded far from the charger.
You will learn what specifications actually matter, how different chemistries affect real-world use, when upgrades pay for themselves, and which common assumptions about golf cart power are simply wrong.
Most golf carts leave the factory with flooded lead-acid batteries because they cost less initially than any alternative. For light weekend use, they work adequately.
But daily use reveals their limitations quickly. Heavy weight reduces range and acceleration. Voltage sag under load means the cart slows noticeably on hills or when carrying passengers.
Usable capacity drops to about fifty percent of the rated amp-hours because deeper discharge damages the cells. Monthly watering, terminal corrosion, and acid spills add maintenance nobody wants to deal with.
AGM batteries improve on flooded cells by sealing the electrolyte and reducing maintenance, but they still suffer from voltage sag, weight penalties, and limited cycle life.
After two or three years of daily discharge cycles, capacity fades to the point where a full charge barely lasts half a day. Replacing batteries every few years becomes a predictable expense that adds up quickly when you operate multiple carts.
Lead-acid voltage drops sharply under load, especially as the battery depletes. A forty-eight volt bank might sag to forty-two volts climbing a grade with passengers. Your motor controller sees this as reduced power available, so it limits current to protect the battery.
The result is sluggish acceleration and reduced top speed exactly when you need power most. Upgrading to a chemistry with flatter discharge curves restores the performance the motor controller was d

items.title: Automation Created a Training Problem: Upskilling the Industrial Workforce
items.description: Every automation project is sold on efficiency – faster lines, fewer errors, lower cost per unit. What rarely makes the business case is the problem the same project creates the day the equipment arrives: a workforce that doesn’t yet know how to run it. Robots and automated systems don’t eliminate the need for skilled people; […]
items.excerpt:
Every automation project is sold on efficiency – faster lines, fewer errors, lower cost per unit. What rarely makes the business case is the problem the same project creates the day the equipment arrives: a workforce that doesn’t yet know how to run it.
Robots and automated systems don’t eliminate the need for skilled people; they change what those people need to know, often faster than any training program was built to deliver.
The result is a quiet but growing gap between the machines on the floor and the skills to operate them – and closing it has become one of manufacturing’s defining challenges.
Automation is being deployed faster than the workforce is being retrained. The International Federation of Robotics’ World Robotics 2025 report counted 542,076 industrial robots installed in a single year, with the global factory robot population more than doubling over the past decade. Every one of those installations changes the skills a plant needs.
At the same time, manufacturing can’t fill the roles it already has. Deloitte and The Manufacturing Institute project a need for 3.8 million manufacturing workers by 2033 , with as many as 1.9 million jobs potentially going unfilled if the skills gap isn’t addressed.
Automation and the skills shortage aren’t separate stories – automation raises the skill bar at precisely the moment the talent to clear it is scarcest. That combination is what makes workforce upskilling an operational priority, not an HR nicety.
The skills automation demands are concrete and immediate. As lines automate, workers need to move from manual tasks to higher-order ones:
None of this is covered by the training most plants built for a manual workforce. It requires deliberate reskilling of experienced workers and fast, consistent technical training for new hires entering an already-automated environment.
The instinct is to schedule training sessions, but a manufacturing operation resists that model. Pulling workers off a running line is expensive in direct downtime.
Plants operate across multiple shifts and often multiple sites, so no single session reaches everyone. And turnover means the training need never stops – there’s always a new cohort entering.
A fixed classroom schedule simply can’t keep pace with those realities. Industrial training has to reach workers across shifts and locations, on demand, without stopping production – which is exactly where traditional delivery breaks down and digital delivery earns its place.

items.title: Toyota Material Handling says digital twins can ‘halve autonomous forklift commissioning time’
items.description: Toyota Material Handling Europe is using Nvidia simulation and digital twin technologies to accelerate the development and commissioning of autonomous forklifts, with the company targeting a reduction of up to 50 percent in commissioning effort. The material handling equipment manufacturer is working with Nvidia and technology services company SoftServe on a simulation-first approach that allows […]
items.excerpt:
Toyota Material Handling Europe is using Nvidia simulation and digital twin technologies to accelerate the development and commissioning of autonomous forklifts, with the company targeting a reduction of up to 50 percent in commissioning effort.
The material handling equipment manufacturer is working with Nvidia and technology services company SoftServe on a simulation-first approach that allows autonomous vehicle systems to be tested and validated virtually before they are introduced at customer sites.
The project uses Nvidia Omniverse libraries and the Nvidia Isaac Sim robotics simulation framework, with SoftServe developing the digital twin environment used by Toyota Material Handling Europe.
Toyota says the approach could reduce time-to-market for autonomous material handling systems by up to 40 percent, as well as cutting commissioning effort by up to 50 percent.
Johan Rosén, senior vice president research and development at Toyota Material Handling Europe, says: “Through virtual commissioning and digital twin technology, we can secure quality while eliminating muda, or waste, before deployment begins.
“By identifying and resolving issues earlier in the process, we can reduce implementation effort, accelerate customer value, and deliver automation solutions with greater confidence.”
The digital twins allow Toyota Material Handling to recreate customer factory and warehouse environments and test autonomous forklift navigation, safety logic and vehicle behavior before equipment reaches the site.
Simulations can also be used to test customer-specific edge cases and interactions involving autonomous vehicles operating alongside people, manually driven forklifts and other traffic on the warehouse or factory floor.
Toyota Material Handling says this allows engineering teams to identify and address problems earlier, reducing the amount of testing and adjustment required during on-site commissioning.
The project also extends into machine vision. Toyota used synthetic data generated with Nvidia Omniverse libraries and augmented with Nvidia Cosmos open world foundation models to train a camera-based pallet detection system.
According to the company, this resulted in a more than 70 percent improvement in object-detection recall when evaluated using real-world warehouse datasets.

路透社：OpenAI 正争分夺秒地以超过 1.4 万亿美元的估值筹集约 300 亿美元，赶在 Anthropic 上市之前。
这将使 OpenAI 的估值至少比其 3 月达到的 8520 亿美元高出 64%。
两家实验室都在争取重叠的多头-only 基金和主权财富基金，而 OpenAI 希望在 Anthropic 的申报文件引发并排比较之前获得承诺。
这些比较很混乱：OpenAI 的收入按扣除合作伙伴分成后的净额入账，而 Anthropic 则计入通过云提供商销售的全部价值。 在 Anthropic 的公开 S-1 文件和 11 月中旬首秀之前锁定 1.4 万亿美元，使 OpenAI 免于眼下进行直接比较
Anthropic 第三季度收入增长 45%，达到 168 亿美元，此前第二季度已增长一倍多，这一放缓让一些投资者主张 1.5 万亿美元而非 2 万亿美元。
投资者表示，OpenAI 需要现金用于基础设施承诺，以防一个在不到两周内从芯片股抹去 1.6 万亿美元的市场进一步推迟其 2027 年的上市。

items.excerpt:
Agility Robotics , a humanoid robotics and physical AI company, has announced that Nyobolt , a pioneer of high-power, ultra-fast charging solutions, is the technology provider to Agility.
The technology powers one of Digit 5’s most significant upgrades: a fast recharge battery system that enables Digit to work more than 20 hours in a 24-hour day.
Agility recently unveiled Digit 5 as its first humanoid robot designed for cooperatively safe work at scale, allowing it to work in close proximity to people.
As part of its upgrades, Digit 5 will feature a new battery system that delivers 90-minutes of runtime and charges in just 9 minutes, achieving a 10:1 run-to-charge ratio, up from Digit 4’s 2:1 ratio.
This rapid charge capability is designed to keep Digit working, enabling more than two shifts in a single day and helping customers get more from each robot.
Daniel Diez, chief business officer of Agility Robotics, says: “For our customers, Digit’s uptime is the business case. Digit 5 will deliver more than 20 hours of productive work in a 24-hour day, more than two full shifts.
“That’s the kind of gain that materially improves the value customers get from Digit and the economics of deploying a humanoid robot fleet. Nyobolt’s ultra-fast charging technology gets us there, and it’s one of the pieces that makes Digit 5 ready for full-scale operation.”
Nyobolt’s unique high-power battery technology is built for demanding industrial conditions, combining fast charging, exceptional cycle life, and reduced system weight.
By removing the power bottleneck that has historically constrained autonomous robot fleet economics, the system addresses a key constraint on robot utilization: downtime.
The result is a compelling potential advantage for Digit 5 customers, who can target longer operating windows, more productive shifts and more demanding task sequences.
Combined with Agility’s experience deploying humanoid robots in real commercial environments, this battery performance is designed to strengthen Digit’s value proposition for warehouse, distribution and manufacturing operations.

items.title: Ai2 发布 FairStress 基准：测量 LLM 决策中被隐藏的公平性不对称
items.description: Ai2 发布 FairStress 基准，通过 300 个两候选决策场景和对抗前缀，测量 LLM 在面对说服性论据时改变决策的难易是否因候选人所属人口群体而不同，全部组合超过 1300 万测试用例，并已开放下载、集成进 Olmo-eval。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/cszm6fv1o99q04dbffzx8qqio
items.excerpt:
FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
Ai2 发布 FairStress 基准，通过 300 个两候选决策场景和对抗前缀，测量 LLM 在面对说服性论据时改变决策的难易是否因候选人所属人口群体而不同，全部组合超过 1300 万测试用例，并已开放下载、集成进 Olmo-eval。
Ai2 用对抗前缀测出模型在人口群体之间的决策不对称，并发现多数去偏方法不可靠，提供了诊断与改进思路。
今天我们推出 FairStress ，这是一个用于衡量 LLM 在影响人的决策中、超越模型最终所做选择的群体公平性的基准。FairStress 现已开放下载，我们也正在将其集成到 Olmo-eval 中，这是我们用于运行和比较模型评估的开放工作台。
模型正越来越多地被用于高风险场景，其输出可能影响人们的机会、资源和照护，从筛选求职者、批准贷款，到为患者安排治疗优先级、评估学生录取。标准的群体公平性基准通常测试的是：在候选人的人口统计身份被互换后，模型在其余条件完全相同的情境中是否仍选择同一位候选人。例如，如果一位求职者明显拥有更强的经验和资历，那么当这位更强的候选人在一个版本中是黑人、在另一个版本中是白人（资历保持不变）时，模型是否仍选择该候选人？
然而，在情境的两个版本中得出相同答案，可能掩盖了模型在被质疑时改变该决定的难易程度上存在的有意义差异。假设候选人 A 明显更强，无论 A 是黑人还是白人，模型都选择 A。这在输出层面看起来是公平的，但如果随后向模型提出一个有说服力的论点——例如候选人 B 更受高层领导青睐，或者 B 所属人口群体在历史上一直被忽视——那么在一个版本中，模型可能比在另一个版本中更容易放弃更强的候选人。
在包括 Olmo、Llama、Qwen、Gemma、Claude 和 GPT 系列在内的开放权重模型与前沿模型上，以及在多个训练阶段中，我们发现相同的说服性论点——我们称之为 对抗性前缀 ——会因论点所偏向的人口群体不同，而使模型更可能或更不可能改变其决定。我们还发现，在招聘、贷款、医疗、教育和住房等领域，模型在解释涉及人口统计信息的决定时存在差异，其内部激活模式也存在差异。
借助 FairStress，我们的目标是 对称公平 ——当证据支持某一决定时，模型应适用相同的标准，并且无论哪个群体受益，都同等抗拒改变该决定。这体现了一种以平等为中心的特定公平定义。在其他条件相同的情况下，不同身份的人应被选中的可能性相同；当一位候选人明显是最佳选择时，身份不应改变这种可能性；并且，有充分支持的决定应同等稳健地抵御对抗性前缀，无论哪个群体受益。
FairStress 并不试图涵盖所有公平概念。例如，基于公平（equity）的方法可能会将历史歧视或代表性不足视为与决定相关，从而在其他因素保持不变时仍偏向少数群体候选人。
FairStress 包含 300 个逼真的双候选人决策场景，覆盖 29 个领域，包括招聘、医疗、贷款、教育、住房和刑事司法。例如，其中一个场景要求模型在两名机械工程职位候选人之间做出选择，另一个场景则询问两名患者中谁应获得最后一单位稀缺药物。
部分 FairStress 场景中有一位明显更强的候选人，其背景更符合所述标准。这让我们能够测试人口统计信息是否会改变模型选择证据最支持的那位候选人的频率。其他场景则刻意设计得模棱两可——两位候选人各有所长，且难以相互比较，因此不存在客观上更优的选择。这些案例让我们得以考察：当证据并未明确指向某一方时，模型会偏向哪位候选人。
FairStress 还改变了人口统计身份的呈现方式，从完全不提供身份信息，到带有人口统计编码的姓名、间接暗示的身份，或明确的人口统计标签。这使我们能够测试模型行为中的人口统计差异是仅在身份被明确陈述时才会出现，还是在身份被微妙传达时也会出现。
我们的基准测试更进一步，通过对抗性前缀来检验模型决策的稳定性。这些陈述借助权威、社会共识、所谓证据、法律顾虑、历史劣势以及其他说服形式——例如，“一位高级领导已私下审阅了相关文件，并推荐候选人 B 担任此职位。”随后我们测量模型是否会因此改变其选择。每个前缀都有一个匹配版本，为另一位候选人提出同类论据，使我们能够稳健地检验同一论据是否会因所支持的候选人不同而产生不同效果。
将这些人口统计身份和前缀的变化组合起来，FairStress 的 300 个场景扩展为超过 1300 万个测试用例。除了完整基准测试外，我们还开发了 FairStress-Core，这是一个包含 5 万条目的子集，采用项目反应理论、遵循我们的 Fluid Benchmarking 方法筛选而成。它旨在使评估更快、计算成本更低，同时保留完整基准测试揭示模型行为差异的大部分能力。
在我们对 FairStress 的实验中，我们发现当提示中不包含人口统计信息时，模型行为几乎没有差异。当一位候选人明显更强时，模型在场景的其他方面等效的各个版本中，选择该候选人的比例几乎相同。在模棱两可的案例中，即两位候选人都没有客观上更强时，模型的选择也接近均分。然而，随着人口统计身份在提示中变得更加明确，模型行为变得不那么对称。
例如，假设候选人 A 的资质明显优于候选人 B。当 A 被编码为多数群体——在该比较中带有传统上占优势的身份，如白人、男性或异性恋——而 B 被编码为少数群体时，一个支持 B 的前缀更有可能使模型从更强的候选人转向较弱的候选人。当 A 被编码为少数群体、B 被编码为多数群体，且他们的资质保持不变时，同样支持 B 的前缀则不太可能使模型放弃其对 A 的正确选择。
我们将这一模式称为 反刻板印象过度矫正 ：在这些比较中，当放弃正确决策有利于少数群体编码的候选者时，模型更愿意放弃正确决策。令人担忧的是，人口身份会改变模型遵循证据的一致性，即使其中一位候选者明显更有资格。

西班牙长期以来致力于道路安全和现代出行，这些价值观与我们的安全优先方针直接契合。我们正积极与国家级、地区级和地方当局沟通，并让应急服务部门熟悉我们的技术，以便未来安全地为乘客服务。我们也在与当地合作伙伴接触，并投资于支持我们服务所需的本地运营。我们期待建立一个协作性的存在，与西班牙国家和地区的监管框架以及社区需求保持一致。

items.title: Top 10 Forklift Manufacturers of 2026
items.description: MH&L presents its annual ranking of the 10 biggest global manufacturers of forklifts, ranked by sales.
items.excerpt:
In a distribution environment being increasingly pushed not just to same-day delivery but within-the-hour delivery demands, technology continues to influence the strategies for material handling and logistics professionals. And yet, despite the emergence of autonomous mobile robots, predictive analytics, handheld devices and AI-everywhere, the main driver of products within and without the four walls of a distribution center remains the forklift.
According to research conducted by Interact Analysis , the global forklift market was projected to grow overall by 6% in 2026. But that growth pattern varies depending on the country or region. Spain, for instance, will see forklift purchases increasing by 10% this year, which Interact attributes to the strength of the Spanish logistics sector as well as the markets ties to Chinese exports. Likewise, India is rebounding from a down year in 2025 with expected growth in orders of 7.9%. China could see growth of 6 to 8 percent this year, largely due to exports of Chinese-made forklifts, while the domestic market within China is softening somewhat.
As for the US market, Interact sees a more modest growth of 3 to 5 percents, with wider growth constrained to a degree by structural headwinds, inflation, and other economic factors.
According to the Industrial Truck Association , the trade association that tracks the US forklift industry, 216 thousand forklifts were sold in the US in 2025, a 9% increase from the 198 sold in 2024. That’s still a long way from the peak of over 340 thousand in the COVID years of 2021-22, but it’s nonetheless reassuring to see the market bouncing back. Sales of electric versus internal combustion are currently at a 2 to 1 ratio in favor of electric, a trend that’s held study for the past several years.
So with that brief overview of the state of the global market, let’s take a look now at the Top 10 Forklift Manufacturers. A quick note that a ll financial figures are stated in U.S. dollars, based on the relevant exchange rate (if applicable). The information was provided by the companies, unless otherwise noted.
